text_summary.body: In the seventh month the people gathered "as one man" in Jerusalem; Jeshua with the priests and Zerubbabel with his kin built the altar on its base, despite fear of the peoples of the lands; they kept the Feast of Booths and from the first day of the seventh month offered burnt offerings, though the Temple foundation was not yet laid; they paid masons and carpenters and gave food, drink and oil to Sidon and Tyre for cedar brought by sea to Joppa under Cyrus's grant.

setting.body: Batten notes that the passage implies only that the Jerusalem altar had not been restored, not that no sacrifice had been offered anywhere since 586 (against Kosters).

competing_reconstructions.label: Altar in the seventh month of the return year under Cyrus
Altar restored before the 520 rebuilding, the account placed under Cyrus by the Chronicler
competing_reconstructions.summary: Batten keeps the altar restoration early but places the foundation in 520.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik stresses that the altar came before the Temple and that the cedar was a royal "grant" (Kidner).
